title: sec.fix HIGH: check_object_uris accepts path traversal past the prefix (I-22 not enforced)
description: data-security-reviewer HIGH: spine/spine/core/naming.py check_object_uris only tests uri.startswith(prefix) and len>prefix — everything after the canonical prefix s3://<bucket>/<feed>/received_at=.../dl-<delivery_id>/ is unconstrained: '/', '..', '.', '%2e%2e', empty segments all pass. title: sec.fix.residual: pin manifest-object copy (H-1 class) + tighten partner ARN regex (H-3 class)
description:
Two residuals the security-fix agent correctly flagged rather than silently fixing beyond its brief. Both are same-class continuations of HIGH findings, so they close in the security gate rather than deferring.
(1) H-1 residual — the s3-push MANIFEST object's own vestibule->canonical copy is still unpinned. The manifest is read via StoreFx.get_bytes (not stream_sha256), so it never captured a VersionId/ETag, yet it is copied to the canonical prefix and its sha256 recorded in the ledger objects[] list. Same TOCTOU window as H-1: a partner who swaps the manifest between the read and the post-claim copy makes the canonical manifest differ from the one whose completeness assertions were actually verified — the delivery's own source-of-truth assertion document is then unverified in the immutable zone. FIX: have get_bytes return (or additionally expose) the version_id/etag from the same get_object response used for the read, thread it onto the manifest StagedObject exactly as H-1 did for data objects (the fields already exist: src_version_id/src_etag), so the manifest copy is pinned identically. Keep it additive and None-tolerant. Regression test must fail pre-fix: mutate the manifest object between parse and copy, assert the canonical manifest matches the PARSED bytes (or registration fails closed).
(2) H-3 residual — the partner-ARN regex ^arn:aws:iam::[0-9]{12}:(root|role/.+|user/.+)$ accepts an embedded wildcard in the name segment (e.g. role/*). AWS itself rejects wildcard principals of this shape at policy-apply time, so the practical impact is a failed terraform apply rather than an over-grant — but the validator should reject it at the config gate where the error is cheap and legible. FIX: exclude '*' (and whitespace) from the role/user name segment; add tests for role/*, user/*, and a legitimate path-prefixed role (role/path/name must still be accepted).
Files: ingestion/ingestion/effects/s3.py, ingestion/ingestion/effects/records.py, ingestion/ingestion/drivers/s3_push.py, ingestion/ingestion/core/model.py, and the corresponding tests under ingestion/tests/. Do NOT touch ingestion/terraform/**.
acceptance_criteria: make lint schemas registry test coverage green from ingestion/ (>=347 tests, coverage gates hold); manifest-mutation regression test present and proven to fail against pre-fix behavior; ARN regex tests cover wildcard rejection and path-prefixed acceptance.
notes: verified+closed: manifest copy now pinned via get_bytes_pinned (VersionId+ETag from the same GetObject used for the read); ARN regex excludes wildcard/whitespace in the name segment while keeping path-prefixed roles. Agent caught that a naive revert bypasses the mutation hook and yields a false-negative pass — constructed a revert that actually reproduces the defect. Two new caveats journaled: core/decisions.py docstring now stale re: manifest pin fields; Python bare $ anchor laxity in the ARN regex (pre-existing, out of scope).

title: sec.fix.code: H-1 TOCTOU, H-2/H-4 pydantic error leakage, H-3 ARN validation, M-1 resume grant, M-2 bucket trust, M-9 logging
description:
Security-gate fixes, PYTHON ONLY (ingestion/ingestion/**, ingestion/tests/**). Terraform is a sibling bead — do not touch ingestion/terraform/**.
H-1 (HIGH, TOCTOU: drivers/s3_push.py hash sites, effects/s3.py copy_verbatim, registration/registrar.py copy step): stream_sha256 hashes the vestibule object at T0; the server-side copy happens at T1 after the CAS claim; the partner retains PutObject on incoming/* and the bucket is versioned, so bytes can be swapped in between — the ledger then records a content_hash/batch_id describing bytes that are NOT what landed in the lake. FIX: capture VersionId when hashing (head_object/get_object response), thread it through ObjectSummary -> StagedObject (additive optional field) -> CopySpec, and pass CopySource={Bucket,Key,VersionId} in copy_verbatim (CopySourceIfMatch=<etag> is an acceptable fallback where no version is available). Keep it additive and None-tolerant so the sftp-pull path (src_key=None) is unaffected. Add a golden/integration test that mutates the vestibule object between hash and copy and asserts the registered canonical object matches the HASHED bytes (or the registration fails closed) — today it silently copies the new bytes.
H-2 (HIGH, effects/secrets.py ~37): raise TransientError(f"...: {exc}") over a pydantic ValidationError of the SFTP SecretString — pydantic v2 renders input_value, which for top-level errors is the whole decoded secret dict including auth.password. FIX: reduce to (loc, type) only, mirroring tools/put_secret.py::_format_errors; never interpolate str(exc) for a model over secret material. Add a test asserting a known password string never appears in the raised message.
H-4 (HIGH, core/completeness.py ~52 parse_manifest): Defect(reason=str(exc)) over UNTRUSTED partner manifest bytes embeds input_value verbatim; that reason becomes ledger notes — append-only, never deleted, surfaced in Athena named queries — so partner PII lands permanently in the immutable zone, unbounded in length (1000-file manifests). FIX: build the reason from (loc, type) pairs only, no input values, and cap the total length (e.g. first N violations + count). Add a test asserting a distinctive PII-shaped value in a bad manifest never reaches the Defect reason or the resulting ledger row's notes.
H-3 (HIGH, core/model.py S3PushConnection): partner_principal_arns has only min_length=1 — the single field controlling EXTERNAL write access to the landing bucket (D-15) is unvalidated, so a source.yaml PR typo/malice grants a foreign account PutObject on the vestibule. FIX: @field_validator enforcing ^arn:aws:iam::[0-9]{12}:(root|role/.+|user/.+)$ with a distinct error message; tests for valid/invalid forms incl. wildcard and malformed. (The deploy-account allowlist half of this finding is deferred — do not add env plumbing.)
M-1 (MEDIUM but a real functional defect: drivers/sftp_pull.py resume path calls fx.cas.sweep_stale, a DynamoDB Scan, which the per-feed role does not and MUST NOT hold — LeadingKeys cannot constrain Scan, so granting it would break the per-feed CAS blast-radius wall). FIX: add a get_claim(feed_id, batch_id) capability to CasFx backed by GetItem on the exact pk (additive field on the record; wire in effects/cas.py, effects/build.py, tests/conftest.py double) and use it in the sftp resume path instead of sweep_stale. Scan stays exclusively for the absence detector. Extend the resume test to prove no Scan is used (e.g. a double whose scan_stale raises).
M-2 (MEDIUM, drivers/s3_push.py _parse_event and its uses): the registrar trusts the event-supplied bucket name for both the source read AND as the destination bucket in canonical_uri, so a forged event puts an attacker-chosen bucket into StagedObject.uri, ledger object_uris and the delivery-registered payload; sftp_pull correctly uses fx.config.landing_bucket. FIX: reject any event whose bucket != fx.config.landing_bucket (log ERROR, return, same shape as the existing misroute path), and pass fx.config.landing_bucket into canonical-URI construction. Add a golden test asserting a foreign-bucket event registers nothing.
M-9-code (observability.py + entrypoints/*): make_json_handler is defined and unit-tested but called from NOWHERE, so section 11.1 structured logging with feed_id/delivery_id correlation is not actually in effect in any deployed function. FIX: install it on the root logger once per entrypoint (all four), guarded against duplicate handlers on warm invocations; add a test asserting a handler is installed exactly once across two handler invocations. Also address L-7 while here: absence/detector.py logs the whole ClaimItem repr at WARNING — reduce to feed_id/batch_id/status.
acceptance_criteria: Full CI line green from ingestion/: make lint schemas registry test coverage (test count >= 323 + new tests, coverage gates hold); new tests present for each of H-1/H-2/H-3/H-4/M-1/M-2/M-9; grep confirms no remaining str(ValidationError) interpolation over secret or partner-controlled models.
notes: coordinator verified: 347 tests green, coverage 91.8/99.6, all 7 findings fixed with revert-proven regression tests (M-2's test showed the OLD code actually registered deliveries pointing into an attacker bucket — stronger proof than a crash). H-1 threads VersionId+ETag from hash through to CopySource. Honest limits stated: moto does not enforce CopySourceIfMatch so the unversioned fallback is unverifiable locally. TWO RESIDUALS promoted to a closing fix bead rather than deferred (security gate: HIGH residuals do not defer).

title: sec.fix.iac: C-1 lake privilege escalation, M-3/M-5/M-6/M-9/M-10 (terraform only)
description:
Security-gate fixes, TERRAFORM ONLY (ingestion/terraform/**). Full finding text is in the security report; each item below is normative.
C-1 (CRITICAL, platform/iam.tf ~24-50): ledger_write and ledger_read grant s3:Get*/Put*/List* with the LAKE BUCKET ARN in the resource list, so s3:Put* covers bucket-level actions — PutBucketPolicy, PutBucketPublicAccessBlock, PutBucketAcl, PutEncryptionConfiguration, PutBucketVersioning on the lake bucket. Registrar compromise => make the ledger public/deletable, bypassing D-9 without ever holding s3:DeleteObject. FIX: split each into object actions (s3:GetObject/s3:PutObject, and only those needed) on "${lake.arn}/ledger/*" PLUS s3:ListBucket on lake.arn with condition StringLike s3:prefix = ["ledger/*"]. Copy the shape from modules/feed/iam.tf (which is already correct). AUDIT every other statement in platform/iam.tf for the same bucket-ARN-in-object-statement pattern — the reviewer calls it a copy-paste class, not a one-off.
M-10 (platform/iam.tf ~92-96): registrar s3:ListBucket on the whole landing bucket unconditioned — can enumerate every feed's canonical received_at= tree. FIX: s3:GetObject on "${landing}/*/incoming/*"; s3:ListBucket on landing.arn with StringLike s3:prefix = ["*/incoming/*"].
M-3 (platform/iam.tf ~98-102, feed/iam.tf ~38-42, platform/s3.tf lifecycle): effects/s3.py's stream_upload aborts multipart on failure but NO role holds s3:AbortMultipartUpload — the abort raises AccessDenied from inside the except block, masking the real error, and orphaned parts bill forever. FIX: add s3:AbortMultipartUpload + s3:ListMultipartUploadParts to registrar and feed roles on the received_at= resources, AND add abort_incomplete_multipart_upload { days_after_initiation = 7 } to the landing lifecycle configuration.
M-5 (platform/iam.tf lambda_assume/scheduler_assume, feed/iam.tf trust): bare service-principal trusts. FIX: add condition StringEquals aws:SourceAccount = account id to all three trust documents; add aws:SourceArn scoped to arn:aws:scheduler:REGION:ACCOUNT:schedule/* on scheduler_assume.
M-6 (feed/s3_push.tf ~67-74): the s3-push EventBridge target has NO retry_policy and NO dead_letter_config, unlike every scheduler target. Under burst + the registrar's reserved concurrency of 10, EventBridge throttles, retries 24h, then DROPS — no ledger row, no DLQ, no alarm. This violates the project invariant 'quarantine with reasons, never silent drops'. FIX: add dead_letter_config { arn = var.platform.dlq_arn } and retry_policy { maximum_event_age_in_seconds = 3600, maximum_retry_attempts = 5 }.
M-9-tf (platform/lambda.tf, feed/sftp_pull.tf): function log groups are not declared, so they auto-create with NEVER EXPIRE retention while receiving delivery keys, filenames, ClaimItem reprs and error strings. FIX: declare aws_cloudwatch_log_group "/aws/lambda/<name>" with retention_in_days (use 30, or a variable defaulting to 30) for all four function shapes (registrar, absence, maintenance, per-feed driver); make sure the functions depend on them so Lambda does not race-create.
Do NOT change: bucket SSE (M-8) or anything requiring a CMK; the name-convention wildcards (M-4); .gitignore/Dockerfile (M-7) — all deferred to separate beads.
acceptance_criteria: terraform fmt -check -recursive and terraform validate green for modules/platform, modules/feed, and envs/dev (run terraform init -backend=false first); grep audit shows no remaining statement pairing a bucket ARN with Put*/Get*/List* object-action wildcards; the Python test suite is untouched and still green (make test).
notes: verified+closed by coordinator: C-1 split (object actions on ledger/* + conditioned ListBucket), M-10 same treatment, M-3 abort-MPU grants + 7d lifecycle, M-5 SourceAccount/SourceArn on all three trusts, M-6 DLQ+retry, M-9 four log groups w/ 30d retention. Agent added terraform test files (.tftest.hcl) with revert-proven red states — good practice, kept. NOTABLE CATCH: agent found the M-6 dead_letter_config would be SILENTLY INERT without an SQS resource policy admitting events.amazonaws.com (rule targets deliver as service principal, unlike Lambda/Scheduler DLQs which are identity-based) — added aws_sqs_queue_policy scoped by aws:SourceAccount. That completion is exactly the finding's intent. Grep audit: no remaining bucket-ARN/object-action wildcard pairs.

title: Errata pass: 006/007/004.1 register updates from the 2026-08-20 v1.0 review

title: [M1] Folds, candidate selection, and the pure registration planners
description:
Implement the ledger read-model and all decision logic as pure functions. `core/folds.py` (§7.4 normative): latest_dispositions (group by delivery_id, max (recorded_at, disposition-rank); tie rank unreadable > superseded > duplicate > incomplete > registered), registered_deliveries, feed_watermark, acquired_final (every object INCLUDING role=manifest, for latest disposition in {registered, duplicate, superseded} — superseded stays acquired), observed_defective (single-object trailer/timer deliveries only; manifest-mode deliberately excluded — they are re-examined manifest-first each run). `core/windows.py` (§7.4): RemoteFile; select_candidates (fnmatch pattern → drop (name,bytes) ∈ acquired ∪ defective unless force → timer quiet-window filter → sort (mtime, name) ascending; force=True bypasses only step 2, D-16); select_manifests (non-final manifests re-examined every run by design). `core/decisions.py` (§8.3 normative, §8, §9.4): define RegistrationRequest here (§8.1 — its CompletenessResult field is why it lives here, not model.py), CopySpec, RegistrationPlan; plan_registration building plans per the claim.kind table — WON (registered row + superseded accretion row when a registered prior with same delivery_key and different content_hash exists in the fold of prior rows; copies from StagedObjects with src_key set; event; complete_claim), LOST_COMPLETED and LOST_IN_PROGRESS (one duplicate row each — both sides of every race are remembered, no event/copies), TAKEN_OVER (plan rebuilt entirely from claim.item — the dead run's delivery_id/received_at/inventory — byte-identical to what the dead run would have executed; supersession detection runs here too); every row obeys the §6.2 population table exactly. plan_nondelivery with the append-on-change rule (§8: latest row for this delivery_key has same disposition AND same observed (name,bytes) inventory → rows=(); never copies/event/claim). plan_reconciliation (§9.4 step 3: delivery_keys with >1 live registered → superseded accretion rows for all but newest received_at; idempotent). Do NOT attempt to fix the concurrent-correction race in the planner (§8.3: both racers may compute supersedes=None; reconciliation repairs it — a delivery_key lock was explicitly rejected). Unit tests: fold idempotence property latest_dispositions(rows+rows)==latest_dispositions(rows) (§12.3), rank tiebreak, acquired/defective set semantics, selection with force and quiet window, one plan test per claim.kind, append-on-change suppression, TAKEN_OVER identity adoption. Parallel with m1-core-verifiers — do not touch hashing/minting/completeness/expectations files.

title: [M0] Purity + idiom linter with self-tests
description:
Implement `tools/purity_linter.py` per LLD §12.2 (rule lists are normative) enforcing the §7.0/D-17 idiom. Stdlib `ast` walk over `ingestion/**/*.py` and `sources/**/*.py`. Two rule groups. PURITY (applies to `ingestion/core/**` and `sources/**`; effects/entrypoints exempt): banned imports — module or any submodule, including `from os.path import join` and aliased forms — boto3, botocore, pyiceberg, paramiko, requests, urllib, http, socket, subprocess, os, sys, io, pathlib, sqlite3, random, tempfile, threading, multiprocessing, time; banned calls (attribute-resolved best-effort): open, eval, exec, __import__, datetime.now/utcnow/today, date.today, uuid.uuid1, uuid.uuid4 (uuid5 allowed — 'now' is always a parameter); ban `raise` and `try` statements. IDIOM (applies to ALL of ingestion/** and sources/**, no exemptions): `class` statements banned unless @dataclass(frozen=True)-decorated, pydantic BaseModel subclass, or enum.Enum subclass (pydantic validators allowed); banned imports anywhere: toolz, cytoolz, returns, pyrsistent, funcy, effect, unittest.mock. Output `file:line:rule`, nonzero exit on any violation. CRITICAL DESIGN POINT: include exactly one hardcoded allowlist entry permitting the `try` in `ingestion/core/completeness.py::parse_manifest` — §7.3 names it 'the ONE place a pydantic exception is caught-and-reified' while §12.2 bans try in core; the allowlist is the smallest resolution of that contradiction. Hardcode it with a comment citing both sections; do NOT build a config/pragma mechanism. Ship unit tests with pass/fail fixture files (`tests/unit/purity_fixtures/`) covering: banned submodule from-import, aliased import, nested class, both `@dataclass(frozen=True)` and `dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)` spellings, pydantic validator methods allowed, unittest.mock ban, the parse_manifest allowlist. The Makefile already invokes the linter in `make lint` — do not modify the Makefile. The linter itself must satisfy its own idiom rules. Do NOT add auto-fix, plugins, or configurability.

FILES (ownership): ingestion/tools/purity_linter.py, ingestion/tests/unit/test_purity_linter.py, ingestion/tests/unit/purity_fixtures/
